title: When the Restaurant Line Is the Hotel Line
summary: More than half of the hotels in Germany, Austria and Switzerland lead with their restaurant. Where one number serves both, a room inquiry lands on the restaurant's line.
body_markdown:
Common questions


## FAQ


### What is a Gasthof, and how is it different from a hotel?


A Gasthof is usually a rural restaurant business that serves food and drink and also keeps some rooms, in the wording of the Deutsche Hotelklassifizierung. DEHOGA defines a hotel as a lodging business offering at least reception, accommodation, daily cleaning, additional services, and at least one restaurant for house guests and passers-by, and says a hotel should have more than 20 rooms.


The Gasthof starts from the restaurant. The hotel starts from the rooms and includes a restaurant.


### What is a Hotel garni?


A Hotel garni is a hotel that offers rooms, breakfast, drinks and at most small meals, in DEHOGA's definition. It is the named exception in German-speaking hospitality, where a hotel by definition includes at least one restaurant for house guests and passers-by. Because a garni has no restaurant, its phone serves the rooms alone.


### How many hotels in Germany, Austria and Switzerland have their own restaurant?


A scan of 26,707 hotels with a website across Germany, Austria and Switzerland measured a narrower group: 55.4% show their own restaurant and a substantial food offer on their website and are classed as food-led. The figure reads website signals, not revenue, and covers the three countries together, not Germany alone. Hotels without a website are outside the scan.


The share of hotels with any restaurant at all is not what the scan measured.


### What happens when a hotel's restaurant and rooms share one phone number?


A room inquiry reaches whoever the restaurant has free, during the hours the restaurant keeps. At least 12.8% of 26,707 hotels in Germany, Austria and Switzerland state on their own website that the restaurant number is the hotel number. That is a floor, because only houses that say so are counted.


The guest calling about a room cannot tell that the line is also taking table reservations, so what that guest gets depends on who owns room calls during service and on rest days.


### Should a Gasthof have a separate phone number for room bookings?


A second number helps only if someone answers it during service and on the rest day. The decision that matters is who owns room calls while the restaurant is busy or closed, and what happens to an inquiry that cannot be settled on the spot. With one number, publish the hours it takes room calls.


With either setup, test it by calling during lunch, during dinner and on the rest day.


### Does a restaurant rest day mean the hotel cannot be reached?


Not by itself. A weekly rest day closes the dining room, and at least 8.7% of 26,707 hotels in Germany, Austria and Switzerland publish one. Whether the phone keeps the rest day too is a separate decision. In a house with one number for the restaurant and the rooms, it is made by default unless someone decides who takes room calls that day.
